record.paper: Many flows in the group connectivity setting

dossier_meta.paper: Many flows in the group connectivity setting
dossier_meta.statement_text: There exists a fixed constant $c > 1$ so that the following holds. For every 3-edge-connected oriented graph $G = (V, E)$ of order $n$, every abelian group $\Gamma$ with $|\Gamma| \geq 6$, and every $f : E \to \Gamma$, there exist at least $c^n$ flows $\phi : E \to \Gamma$ with $\phi(e) \neq f(e)$ for every $e \in E$.
dossier_meta.context_text: Theorem 1.9 establishes an explicit exponential lower bound on the number of $\Gamma$-connected flows for groups of size $k \geq 8$, but yields only the existence of a single flow for $k = 6, 7$. The authors attribute this gap to a shortcoming of their techniques and conjecture the exponential bound holds for all abelian groups of size at least 6. Theorem 1.9 confirms the conjecture for all groups except $\mathbb{Z}_6$ and $\mathbb{Z}_7$; Theorem 1.11 gives a superpolynomial (but not exponential) lower bound for $\mathbb{Z}_6$.
